The '''Thyrsians '''were a [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] of the [[Near-Human]] [[Echani/Legends|Echani]] originating from the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] world of [[Thyrsus/Legends|Thyrsus]], defined by their differing culture and almost polar-opposite appearance to the Echani. Thyrsians were also known for their role in the development of the [[Force pike/Legends|Force pike]]. The [[Sun Guard]] [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith cult]] arose from the Thyrsians.

==Biology and appearance==
Thyrsians shared few obvious physical similarities with their [[Echani/Legends|Echani]]. Though the two subspecies were widely considered cousins, the Thyrsians' appearance was a diametric contrast to that of the Echani as they were instead known for their dark hair and skin, rather than the white skin and eyes that defined the Echani.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

It was believed that the Echani were the result of [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] experimentation with the [[Human/Legends|Human]] genome, a theory also applied to the Thyrsians as a subspecies.<ref name="GAW" />

==Society and culture==
Thyrsus had long been culturally distinct from the rest of [[Echani/Legends|Echani]] society, maintaining their own stubbornly independent beliefs and traditions that often ran in direct contrast to Echani culture. Thyrsian society was patriarchal, eschewing the female council that governed the [[Six Sisters]]. In combat, Thyrsian warriors were known to favor heavy armor and weapons, such as the [[Force pike/Legends|Force pike]], over the light armor and weaponry favored by the Echani. As with all Echani, Thyrsians were regarded as excellent warriors, and excelled at reading even the smallest cues of body language through the Echani's kinetic communication style.<ref name="GAW" />

The Thyrsians were known as a spiritually restless people. Thyrsians followed a monotheistic solar religion, differing from the lunar religion of the Echani, and Thyrsian military units often wore emblems of the stylised red suns of Thyrsus on their armor. Over one hundred years before the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], the Sun Guard developed a fixation on a prophecy of a messiah figure known as [[Son of Suns/Legends|"the son of suns"]], attracting the attention of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]], who exploited a widespread belief among the Thyrsians that the Sith were the subject of the prophecy to convert the Sun Guards into Sith cultists under the command of [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], and later [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="GAW" />

==History==
Though nominally part of the [[Six Sisters]], a confederation of six worlds dominated by the Echani, the Echani population of the sun-baked world of Thyrsus differed in appearance from their Echani cousins, and were considered by [[Echani Command]] to be stubbornly independent. Thyrsians first emerged onto the galactic stage in [[1154 BBY]], waging a war of independence against [[Echani Command]] during the [[Begali Uprising]]. Though [[Begali]] returned to Echani rule less than a century later, the Thyrsian Sun Guard continued to wage a string of crusades against the Echani until Thyrsian independence was confirmed with the [[Pact of Almera]] in [[899 BBY]]. After the cessation of hostilities between the two Echani cultures, the [[Sun Guard]] warriors that evolved from the ranks of the [[Thyrsian special forces|Thyrsian]] [[Special forces/Legends|special forces]] largely abandoned Thyrsus and soon became military rivals of the similarly seminomadic [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], and the two would clash in numerous battles and wars.<ref name="GAW" /> Most famously, the two warrior cultures participated in the [[Battle of Sintheti|battle for Sintheti]] in [[402 BBY/Legends|402 BBY]], when the two groups were hired by rival claimants to the [[Horned Throne]], with the battle between the two lasting for three years.

The Sun Guard eventually fell under the influence of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]]. During and after their service to [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] used the Sun Guards as sentries, [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] and [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]].<ref name="GAW" /><ref name="Darth P">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Darth Sidious later ordered [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] to task his executor [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] with the elimination of the cult.<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], rogue factions within the Sun Guard were hired by various peoples conquered by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]-aligned planet [[Emberlene]], resulting in the [[Destruction of Emberlene|destruction of the world]].

Thyrsian society was divided by the rise of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Most Thyrsians were strong supporters of the Emperor, and saw the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guard]] as the successors to the Sun Guard, with many Thyrsians winning renown as elite members of the Imperial Army and [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] templates for the Empire's [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtrooper]] units. [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Thyrsians, particularly members of the Sun Guard, became candidates for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Shadow Guard]].<ref name="GAW" /> However, many Thyrsians contended that the Sith had misled them, and sought to revive the Sun Guard.

Thyrsus became an isolationist world after the Emperor's demise, with the Thyrsians resisting the entreaties of various Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] as well as the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].
